regions.Chattanooga: A compact river city: the Hunter Museum and Walnut Street Bridge, the Tennessee Aquarium, and Lookout Mountain's Incline, Ruby Falls and Point Park.
regions.Cumberland Plateau: Waterfall country: Fall Creek, Burgess and Cummins Falls, Sewanee's Gothic campus, Sergeant York's farm and the English utopia of Rugby by Big South Fork.
regions.East Tennessee and the Smokies: Knoxville's museums and Sunsphere, Oak Ridge's Manhattan Project history, the Museum of Appalachia, and the Great Smoky Mountains with Cades Cove.
regions.Memphis: Music and civil rights: Graceland, Sun and Stax, Beale Street and the Peabody ducks, and the National Civil Rights Museum at the Lorraine Motel.
regions.Nashville and Middle Tennessee: The Country Music Hall of Fame, the Ryman and Studio B, the new National Museum of African American Music, the Parthenon and the Frist, with the Hermitage and Franklin nearby.
regions.West Tennessee: Shiloh battlefield and Pinson Mounds, Tina Turner's school in Brownsville and Alex Haley's Henning, with eagles at Reelfoot Lake in winter.

sites.name: Graceland
sites.desc: Elvis Presley's home, preserved with its Jungle Room, and a large exhibition complex across the street.

sites.name: Sun Studio
sites.desc: The small studio where Sam Phillips recorded Elvis, Johnny Cash and early rock and roll and blues.

sites.name: Stax Museum of American Soul Music
sites.desc: On the site of Stax Records in Soulsville, home of Otis Redding, Isaac Hayes and Booker T. and the MGs.
sites.wiki: Stax Museum of American Soul Music

sites.name: National Civil Rights Museum
sites.desc: Built around the Lorraine Motel, where Martin Luther King Jr. was killed in 1968.

sites.name: Memphis Rock 'n' Soul Museum
sites.desc: A Smithsonian-developed museum of the music of Memphis.

sites.name: Blues Hall of Fame
sites.desc: The Blues Foundation's museum of inductees, near the Civil Rights Museum.

sites.name: Beale Street
sites.desc: The street where W. C. Handy and B. B. King played, now lined with blues clubs.

sites.name: The Peabody Ducks
sites.desc: The grand 1925 hotel where ducks march to the lobby fountain every morning at 11.

sites.name: Memphis Brooks Museum of Art
sites.desc: Tennessee's oldest and largest art museum, with collections from antiquity to today.

sites.name: Dixon Gallery and Gardens
sites.desc: French Impressionist paintings and gardens in a former Memphis estate.

sites.name: Metal Museum
sites.desc: Museum of fine metalwork on a Mississippi bluff, with a working foundry.

sites.name: Chucalissa
sites.desc: A Mississippian mound site and museum run by the University of Memphis.

sites.name: Shiloh National Military Park
sites.desc: The battlefield of April 1862, with prehistoric mounds above the Tennessee River.

sites.name: Pinson Mounds
sites.desc: Middle Woodland ceremonial mounds, including Sauls' Mound, one of the tallest in the country.

sites.name: Casey Jones Home and Railroad Museum
sites.desc: The Jackson home of the engineer of ballad fame.

sites.name: Tina Turner Museum at Flagg Grove School
sites.desc: The one-room school Tina Turner attended, moved to Brownsville and opened as a museum.

sites.name: Alex Haley Museum
sites.desc: The Henning boyhood home of the author of Roots.

sites.name: Reelfoot Lake State Park
sites.desc: A cypress swamp lake formed by the New Madrid earthquakes of 1811 and 1812, with wintering bald eagles.

sites.name: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
sites.desc: The great museum of country music, with Hatch Show Print and tours to RCA Studio B.
sites.wiki: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum

sites.name: Ryman Auditorium
sites.desc: Built in 1892 as a tabernacle and home of the Grand Ole Opry from 1943 to 1974.

sites.name: RCA Studio B
sites.desc: Where the Nashville Sound was recorded, from Elvis to Dolly Parton.

sites.name: National Museum of African American Music
sites.desc: Opened in 2021, tracing more than 50 genres from spirituals to hip hop.
sites.wiki: National Museum of African American Music

sites.name: Johnny Cash Museum
sites.desc: The largest collection of Johnny Cash artifacts.

sites.name: Musicians Hall of Fame and Museum
sites.desc: Honors session players behind famous records.
sites.wiki: Musicians Hall of Fame and Museum

sites.name: Frist Art Museum
sites.desc: Changing exhibitions in Nashville's 1934 Art Deco post office.

sites.name: Tennessee State Museum
sites.desc: Free state history museum by the Bicentennial Capitol Mall.

sites.name: The Parthenon, Centennial Park
sites.desc: A full-scale replica of the Athenian Parthenon from 1897, now an art museum with a 42 foot Athena.

sites.name: Tennessee State Capitol
sites.desc: William Strickland's Greek Revival capitol (1859); the architect is entombed in its walls.

sites.name: Belle Meade Historic Site
sites.desc: A Greek Revival plantation house and thoroughbred farm, interpreted with the lives of the enslaved.

sites.name: Cheekwood
sites.desc: A 1929 country estate with botanical gardens and an art museum.
sites.wiki: Cheekwood Botanical Garden and Museum of Art

sites.name: Lane Motor Museum
sites.desc: Quirky European cars, microcars and prototypes in a former bakery.

sites.name: Grand Ole Opry House
sites.desc: The Opry's home since 1974, with a circle of wood from the Ryman stage.

sites.name: The Hermitage
sites.desc: Andrew Jackson's plantation, interpreted including the people enslaved there.

sites.name: Radnor Lake State Park
sites.desc: A wildlife refuge with lake trails inside the city.

sites.name: Carter House, Franklin
sites.desc: Farmhouse still marked by bullets from the 1864 Battle of Franklin.

sites.name: Natchez Trace Parkway
sites.desc: A scenic parkway on an old trade route, with the Double Arch Bridge near its northern end.

sites.name: Jack Daniel's Distillery
sites.desc: The Tennessee whiskey distillery in Lynchburg, in a dry county.

sites.name: Fall Creek Falls State Park
sites.desc: Gorges and cascades led by a waterfall of about 256 feet.

sites.name: Burgess Falls State Park
sites.desc: A series of waterfalls on the Falling Water River.

sites.name: Cummins Falls State Park
sites.desc: A swimming hole waterfall reached by wading up the gorge, permit required.

sites.name: University of the South, Sewanee
sites.desc: A Gothic Revival campus on the Cumberland Plateau, with All Saints' Chapel.
sites.wiki: Sewanee: The University of the South

sites.name: Sgt. Alvin C. York State Historic Park
sites.desc: The farm and mill of the World War I hero at Pall Mall.
sites.wiki: Sgt. Alvin C. York State Historic Park

sites.name: Historic Rugby
sites.desc: A Victorian village founded in 1880 by Thomas Hughes as an English utopian colony.

sites.name: Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area
sites.desc: Gorges, arches and river trails on the Tennessee and Kentucky border.
sites.wiki: Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area

sites.name: Hunter Museum of American Art
sites.desc: American art set on a bluff above the Tennessee River.

sites.name: Tennessee Aquarium
sites.desc: Freshwater and ocean aquariums on the riverfront, the anchor of Chattanooga's revival.

sites.name: Walnut Street Bridge
sites.desc: An 1891 truss bridge turned pedestrian walkway, among the longest in the world.

sites.name: Bessie Smith Cultural Center
sites.desc: African American history and the legacy of the Empress of the Blues, born in Chattanooga.

sites.name: Ruby Falls
sites.desc: A 145 foot underground waterfall inside Lookout Mountain.

sites.name: Lookout Mountain Incline Railway
sites.desc: One of the steepest passenger railways in the world, running since 1895.

sites.name: Point Park, Lookout Mountain
sites.desc: Civil War battlefield park at the top of Lookout Mountain with views over Chattanooga.

sites.name: Museum of Appalachia
sites.desc: John Rice Irwin's farm village of log buildings and everyday objects of mountain life.

sites.name: Norris Dam
sites.desc: The TVA's first dam (1936), with modernist design by Roland Wank.

sites.name: Manhattan Project National Historical Park, Oak Ridge
sites.desc: The secret city built in 1942 to enrich uranium, with tours from the American Museum of Science and Energy.

sites.name: Knoxville Museum of Art
sites.desc: Free museum with a monumental glass installation by Richard Jolley.

sites.name: Sunsphere
sites.desc: The gold glass sphere tower of the 1982 World's Fair, with a free observation deck.

sites.name: McClung Museum
sites.desc: The University of Tennessee's museum of archaeology, natural history and decorative arts.
sites.wiki: McClung Museum of Natural History and Culture

sites.name: Blount Mansion
sites.desc: The 1792 frame house of territorial governor William Blount.

sites.name: Dollywood
sites.desc: Dolly Parton's theme park in Pigeon Forge, with Appalachian crafts and music.

sites.name: Cades Cove
sites.desc: A mountain valley loop with log cabins, churches and wildlife in the Smokies.

sites.name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
sites.desc: The most visited national park in the country. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
